## Acceptance criteria

REQ-01 and REQ-02 fail: the generated projection omits `config validate`’s warning exit and mischaracterizes default `serve`. REQ-03 also remains unmet because command documentation still hand-copies projected outcomes.

## Architecture and separation of concerns

No new domain/storage/command boundary violation found.

## Functional paradigm

No blocking functional-style issue found.

## Correctness and invariants

The exit-code reference is inaccurate for two runtime paths; see F1–F2.

## Safety

No unsafe code or PID-safety regression found.

## Testing

The recorded `cargo-ci` gate passed (`fmt`, `clippy`, and 3619 tests); per instruction, I did not rerun tests. Repository validation passed. The new tests do not follow the required naming convention and do not detect the `serve` drift.

## Error handling and CLI contract

No separate error-handling or JSON-contract issue found.

## Documentation

The generated reference is discoverable, but CLI documentation still duplicates command-specific mappings rather than citing the generated source.

## JIT issue management

The prerequisite `6d82de03` is done, and `./scripts/jit-validate.sh` passed.

1. **F1 — High:** The projection omits `config validate` exit `2` for warnings. Runtime exits `2` whenever warnings exist without errors at [main.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/main.rs:5525), but [schema.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/schema.rs:847) now documents only exit `1`. This makes the generated reference incomplete and violates REQ-01/REQ-02.

2. **F2 — High:** The `serve` pass-through row is inaccurate and not mechanically verified. [schema.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/schema.rs:875) presents all `serve` invocations as child-code pass-through, but that behavior exists only in foreground mode at [main.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/main.rs:6529). The default daemon path converts a child startup exit into an error at [serve.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:477), which dispatch then exits as `1`. The purported test only reasserts the schema row at [command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/tests/command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs:286), so runtime drift cannot fail it. This fails REQ-01 and REQ-02.

3. **F3 — High:** CLI documentation still hand-copies generated command-specific mappings. [cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:2200) manually states the `doc check-links` `0`/`2`/`1` outcomes already owned by the generated reference; similar duplicates remain at lines 1805 and 2997. This leaves a staleness path and fails REQ-03 and the prior-review remediation requirement.

4. **F4 — Medium:** Newly added tests do not follow the mandated `test_<function>_<scenario>` naming convention; for example, [command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/tests/command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs:64) defines `validate_integrity_exit_matches_projection`. This introduces avoidable test-suite convention debt.
